description: Resolution of (system_root_fingerprint, kid) against a manifest view, and the half-open activity window an entry is valid in. Fixes the one obligation of the resolver contract that no digest can express: a resolver MUST answer only from entries already in its view, and MUST NOT expand the manifest on the fly.
why_this_is_a_primitive: Every other vector here pins bytes. This one pins a REFUSAL. A resolver that fetches, derives or invents an entry it does not hold still produces a correct-looking signature verification — the digests all match, and the artifact is accepted under a key no other implementation would have resolved. There is no output to compare, so only a stated case catches it.
resolution_rule: resolve(system_root_fingerprint, kid) answers with the entry stored at EXACTLY that (fingerprint, kid) pair, or an error. A miss on the fingerprint and a miss on the kid are DISTINCT errors: unknown_fingerprint means this resolver has no view of that manifest version at all, unknown_kid means it has the version but not that signing key. An implementation that collapses them loses the operator's ability to tell a wrong manifest from a retired key.
activity_window_rule: An entry is active at reference time t iff valid_from <= t < valid_until — half-open, per system-manifest/1 §15. The instant valid_until is NOT active. Resolution and activity are separate questions: an entry outside its window still RESOLVES (it is in the view) and is reported inactive. A resolver that refuses to resolve an expired entry hides the difference between 'never known' and 'no longer valid'.
non_expansion_invariant: No input to resolve() may cause the resolver's view to grow. The view is fixed when the resolver is built, from the manifest artifact; a resolution attempt is a pure lookup.

manifest_view.note: Two manifest versions, so a cross-version lookup has somewhere wrong to land. Keys are placeholders: this vector fixes resolution behaviour, not key material — the byte contract for keys is in key-derivation/.

resolution_cases.name: present pair resolves
resolution_cases.why: the pair is in the view

resolution_cases.name: second kid in the same version resolves
resolution_cases.why: a manifest version holds several signing keys at once

resolution_cases.name: unknown fingerprint
resolution_cases.why: no view of that manifest version — NOT an unknown kid, even though the kid also does not exist there

resolution_cases.name: known fingerprint, unknown kid
resolution_cases.why: the version is held but does not carry that signing key

resolution_cases.name: cross-version kid is NOT resolved
resolution_cases.why: kid-3 exists, but under fingerprint bbbb… — a resolver keyed on kid alone would wrongly resolve this, accepting a signature from another manifest version

resolution_cases.name: empty kid
resolution_cases.why: absent identifiers do not match a wildcard; there is no default entry

activity_cases.name: at valid_until — NOT active
activity_cases.why: half-open: the upper bound is exclusive. An implementation using <= here keeps a retired key alive for one instant, and two implementations disagree on an artifact signed at exactly that timestamp

activity_cases.name: one second before valid_from — NOT active
expired entry still RESOLVES
activity_cases.why: resolution and activity are separate: the entry is in the view, so it resolves and is reported inactive. Refusing to resolve it would be indistinguishable from never having known it

activity_cases.name: overlapping windows both active
activity_cases.why: kid-1 and kid-2 are both active here — a rotation overlap is normal, and the resolver does not pick one

must_hold: resolve() answers only from entries already in the view; no input causes the view to grow
an unknown fingerprint and an unknown kid are distinct, distinguishable errors
a kid present under a DIFFERENT fingerprint does not resolve
the activity window is half-open: valid_from <= t < valid_until
an entry outside its window resolves and reports inactive, rather than failing to resolve
fingerprint_is_known answers true for every version in the view and false otherwise
